email.subject: Urgent: CHF 2,450.00 is about to leave your account

body.v: We have suspended a transfer of CHF 2,450.00 from your account to an unknown recipient. Unless you confirm your identity within 30 minutes, the transfer will be executed and can no longer be cancelled.
For your security, please do not ignore this message.

hotspots.explain: The address ends in swissalpbank-alerts.example, not swissalpbank.example. Anyone can register a domain name that looks like a bank's.
"Dear customer": your bank knows your name, and uses it.
A large amount and the word "Urgent" right in the subject line: the panic starts before you have even opened the message.
In 30 minutes you cannot check anything. Your bank gives you time, and other ways to reach it.
The button says "Stop the transfer now", but it leads to swissalpbank-secure-login.example, another domain that only looks like the bank's.
A signature takes two seconds to copy. There is nothing suspicious about it in itself, but it proves nothing.

who.prompt: Who is really writing to you? Read the address, not just the name.
who.answer: Someone posing as SwissAlpBank. The display name says SwissAlpBank, but the address is on swissalpbank-alerts.example, which is not the bank's domain.
choices: SwissAlpBank, since the name says so
Your personal adviser at the bank
cues: Compare the sender address with swissalpbank.example.
A display name can be set to anything.

emotion.prompt: Which feeling is this email pressing on?
emotion.answer: Fear and haste: a large sum is about to leave your account and you only have 30 minutes.
choices: Fear of losing money, with a tight deadline
Curiosity about a new offer from the bank
None, it is just a routine notice

ask.prompt: What does it actually want you to do?
ask.answer: Click the link and sign in. Your login details would go straight to whoever wrote the email.
choices: Click a link and sign in
Call the number on the back of your card
Nothing, it is for information only
cues: What does the button lead to?

verify.prompt: How can you check through a channel you control?
verify.answer: Leave the link alone. Open the SwissAlpBank app, or type the bank's address yourself, and look at your recent transactions.
choices: Click the link to see whether it is real
Open the app yourself and check the account
Reply to the email to ask for confirmation
cues: A channel you control is one you open yourself, not one the email gives you.

actions.label: Open the SwissAlpBank app yourself and look at your recent transactions
actions.consequence: No transfer is pending. The email was fake, and you gave nothing away.

actions.label: Click "Stop the transfer now" and sign in
actions.consequence: The page looks just like your bank's, but your login details go to the scammer, who can now get into your account.

actions.label: Reply to ask whether the email is genuine
actions.consequence: The scammer assures you it is and pushes even harder. Along the way, they learn that your address is active.

actions.label: Report the email as phishing and delete it
actions.consequence: You clicked nothing, and your mail service learns to filter out similar emails.

attacker_reveal: I copied the bank's name, chose an address close enough and made up the transfer. The 30 minutes were there so you would click before checking: on my page, your password would have come straight to me.
